text:
maria: Quick follow-up on the dedicated GPU pool autoscaling RFC — ran the stressbench overnight and hit two degenerate cases we didn’t fully account for.

maria: 1) long tail of tiny requests causing many tiny scale-ups, 2) burst lane exhausts when multiple tenants do ramped inference (function call workloads).

sam: Can you paste the load pattern? were these short seqs (<= 32 tokens) or long?

maria: Mostly short. 70% < 64 tokens, lots of concurrent cold starts. Peak qps was around 2.4k but sustained at 300-400 for 20m.

jen: two quick thoughts: increase prefix caching for hot tenants AND cap reactive ramp per-tenant. Also add a circuit breaker for pool-level burst drain.

alex: +1. We should avoid spinning up whole MIGs for microbursts. Need admission smoothing on the control plane side.

leo: experiment result — when we set headroom_ratio=0.2 and prewarm_credit=3, cold starts dropped by ~40% but costs went up ~12%. tradeoff as expected.

maria: That matches. We need a formalizable policy surface so ops can tune per-customer without touching core autoscaler. Suggest: per-tenant soft_max, burst_quota, and a global pool circuit breaker.

sam: draft policy snippet for config (for discussion):
```yaml
autoscale_policy: 
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 200
  headroom_ratio: 0.18
  per_tenant:
    default_soft_max: 8
    burst_quota: 5
  burst_lane:
    capacity: 20
    admission_window: 10s
  prewarm_credit: 3
  prewarm_decay: 30m
  pool_circuit_breaker:
    max_concurrent_scale_ops: 4
    cooldown: 2m
```

jen: I like the explicit `pool_circuit_breaker`. It stops the "spin and fail" pattern if nodes are slow to attach. Also recommend telemetry tags: `scale_reason` (latency|throughput|burst) and `tenant_priority` so we can backfill correctly.

alex: operational boundary q: who owns enforcement? operator vs control-plane? If operator enforces admission, control-plane can only propose. We’ve had cross-team confusion here.

maria: proposal: control-plane computes desired delta and records it as an intent. operator executes with its own local guardrails: max_inflight_ops and admission_window. That keeps operator resilient if control-plane is partitioned.

infra-bot: deploy_note: canary autoscaler v2 -> runtime-staging scheduled 11:30 PDT.

leo: we should also tighten metric windows for decisioning. Using 3s windows caused oscillation; move to 15s commit window with exponential backoff for repeated ramps.

sam: agree. Also add a cheap local admission cache: if a tenant recently consumed burst_quota, score them lower for next 2 minutes. Helps fairness.

jen: UX note: expose per-tenant soft_max in console with an override toggle + explain cost impact. This will reduce ticket churn.

maria: Action items: 1) sam — turn draft YAML into an RFC addendum and include backoff parameters (due EOD friday). 2) alex — prototype operator-side `max_inflight_scale_ops` and `cooldown` flags (PR by next Wed). 3) leo — run tuned 24h bench with headroom 0.18 and prewarm=3 and report cost/latency delta.

alex: ack.

sam: ack, will write addendum.

jen: I’ll draft the console wording after we lock defaults.

maria: thanks everyone. if we can ship the circuit breaker early in canary, we can avoid the next noisy outage. :eyes:

infra-bot: canary started: autoscaler-v2 on runtime-staging/zone-a
